---
title: "Systolic Blood Pressure, Age, and Gender Among Adults"
---

## Question

How is mean systolic blood pressure associated with age and gender among adults in the Neighborhood Health Survey?

```{r}
#| message: false
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(broom)

survey <- read_csv(here::here("inputs/raw/neighborhood_health_survey.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
```

## Data

Adults are participants aged 18 and older. Blood pressure was measured only for examined participants, so the analysis keeps adults with a `systolic_mean` value.

```{r}
adults <- survey |>
  filter(age_years >= 18, !is.na(systolic_mean)) |>
  mutate(
    gender = factor(gender, levels = c("male", "female"), labels = c("Female", "Male")),
    gender = relevel(gender, ref = "Male")
  )

n_adults <- sum(survey$age_years >= 18)
n_analyzed <- nrow(adults)
```

The survey has `r format(n_adults, big.mark = ",")` adults. Of these, `r format(n_analyzed, big.mark = ",")` have a blood pressure measurement and are included.

## Summary by gender

```{r}
by_gender <- adults |>
  group_by(gender) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_age = mean(age_years),
    mean_systolic = mean(systolic_mean),
    sd_systolic = sd(systolic_mean)
  )

by_gender
```

## Model

A linear regression of systolic blood pressure on age and gender.

```{r}
fit <- lm(systolic_mean ~ age_years + gender, data = adults)

coefs <- tidy(fit, conf.int = TRUE)
coefs

age_slope <- coefs$estimate[coefs$term == "age_years"]
gender_gap <- coefs$estimate[coefs$term == "genderFemale"]
gender_ci <- coefs[coefs$term == "genderFemale", c("conf.low", "conf.high")]
```

## Figure

```{r}
#| message: false
ggplot(adults, aes(x = age_years, y = systolic_mean, color = gender)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.15, size = 1) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE) +
  labs(
    title = "Systolic blood pressure rises with age; women run higher",
    x = "Age (years)",
    y = "Systolic blood pressure (mm Hg)",
    color = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Interpretation

Systolic blood pressure is associated with age: each additional year is associated with `r round(age_slope, 2)` mm Hg higher systolic pressure, holding gender constant. Women have higher systolic blood pressure than men at every age, by `r round(gender_gap, 1)` mm Hg on average (95% CI `r round(gender_ci$conf.low, 1)` to `r round(gender_ci$conf.high, 1)`). Both associations are large relative to their uncertainty.

The analysis is unweighted and ignores the survey design, so the estimates describe this sample. The data are simulated for teaching.
